sections.description: Introduces the goal to present cross products in two parts: a standard introduction and a deeper linear-algebra perspective, with the first video focusing on main points taught to students.
sections.title: Intro and video plan for cross products

sections.description: Explains that the cross product in 2D corresponds to the area of the parallelogram spanned by V and W, with sign depending on whether V is to the right or left of W.
sections.title: Parallelogram area interpretation in 2D

sections.description: Details how the sign of the cross product depends on vector order, and ties to the standard basis i-hat cross j-hat yielding a positive result when arranged with that orientation.
sections.title: Orientation and basis vectors

concepts: matrix columns as V and W
sections.description: Introduces using a 2x2 determinant with V and W as columns to compute the cross product in 2D and connect to area under a linear transformation.
sections.title: Determinant view for 2D cross product

sections.description: Shows that the determinant gives the area of the parallelogram after transforming the unit square; sign reflects orientation flip.
sections.title: Determinant yields parallelogram area and sign

sections.description: Provides intuition: more perpendicular vectors yield larger parallelogram area; scaling one vector scales the area proportionally.
sections.title: Intuition and scaling properties

sections.description: Clarifies that the true cross product is a vector; its magnitude equals the parallelogram area and direction is perpendicular following the right-hand rule.
sections.title: Cross product is a vector: magnitude and right-hand rule

sections.description: Gives a concrete example: V length 2 in z, W length 2 in y yields cross product of length 4 in the negative x direction.
sections.title: Explicit 2D-to-3D example and result

sections.description: Presents the determinant trick for 3D cross product: place i-hat, j-hat, k-hat in the first column and compute the determinant to get the cross product vector.
sections.title: 3D determinant method with i, j, k basis

sections.description: Explains that treating basis vectors as entries is a notational device that yields a vector perpendicular to V and W; links to a duality concept to be explored in a follow-up video.
sections.title: Why the determinant notation makes sense (duality teaser)

summary: This video introduces the cross product by first revisiting its 2D interpretation as the oriented area of the parallelogram spanned by two vectors, then connects this area to determinants as a computational tool via linear transformations of the basis. It emphasizes that order matters for orientation, demonstrates how to compute 2D cross products using a determinant with V and W as columns, and explains that the true cross product in 3D is a vector whose magnitude equals the parallelogram area and whose direction is perpendicular according to the right-hand rule. A 3D determinant trick using i, j, k bases is introduced to construct the cross product vector, followed by a brief discussion of the rationale behind this notation and a teaser for a deeper geometric interpretation via duality in a subsequent video.
